professional_summary: I've been tuning search clusters since Solr 4 and Elasticsearch 1.x, and I keep getting pulled into the same three problems: shard math nobody did, mappings nobody governed, and heap nobody watched. Today I own Elasticsearch architecture for Capital One's core platform team — 14 clusters, around 300 nodes, roughly 40 TB/day of hot-tier ingest, all queried through a single cross-cluster search (CCS) entry point. The last three years have been mostly semantic work: dense and sparse vector fields, ELSER, kNN/ANN retrieval, RRF blending BM25 with embeddings, rerankers, and RAG pipelines behind a conversational banking assistant. Before Capital One I was on LinkedIn's Elasticsearch/OpenSearch platform team, and before that Netflix's search platform. I read Lucene source when merge policies misbehave, and I've shipped custom Elasticsearch plugins in Java when the query DSL ran out of room. On the infrastructure side it's Terraform, Docker, and Kubernetes across AWS, GCP, and Azure, with Python and Go for everything around the cluster. A big part of the job is sitting with CTOs and enterprise architecture groups explaining why their 500-shard index is the actual problem — I like that part. I also mentor senior engineers; two of the people I coached now run their own search platforms. Happy to travel, since most of my best work happened on-site in a room with the customer's team.

experience.title: Principal Engineer — Search & Retrieval Architecture
bullets: Led Elasticsearch architecture for the core platform org: 14 production clusters, ~300 nodes, and roughly 40 TB/day of hot-tier ingest, all fronted by cross-cluster search (CCS) so product teams hit one endpoint instead of nine

Delivered the bank's first conversational search assistant — hybrid retrieval blending BM25 lexical with dense-vector semantic results through reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), a cross-encoder reranker, and a RAG pipeline now serving 2.1M customer sessions a month

Cut p99 search latency on the account-activity index from 940 ms to 310 ms by rebuilding the analyzer chain (edge n-grams, synonym graph, light_english stemming) and replacing a merge policy that had been copy-pasted since 2018
Rebuilt fleet-wide shard strategy — 4,800 shards down to 1,100 — after cluster state publication started taking 30+ seconds during rolling restarts and stalling every deploy
Moved all time-series indices onto Index Lifecycle Management with hot/warm/cold/frozen tiers backed by S3 searchable snapshots. Annual storage spend dropped about $2.4M.

Set up cross-cluster replication (CCR) between us-east-1 and us-west-2 for the fraud and AML indices, so the regional failover story stopped being a quarterly slide and became something we actually test
Deployed ELSER on dedicated ML nodes for sparse-vector retrieval across 90M policy and disclosure documents, beating the BM25-only baseline by 22 points of nDCG@10 on the internal judgment set
Tuned HNSW parameters (m, ef_construction, num_candidates) for kNN search over 400M 768-dim embeddings and traded 3% recall for a 5x drop in per-query cost
Migrated the legacy Solr-backed retrieval service onto Elasticsearch dense_vector fields, retiring 40 Solr nodes and collapsing two search stacks into one supportable platform
Rewrote merchant search relevance with function_score, rank_features, and pinned queries for merchandising overrides; zero-result rate fell from 11% to 2.8%
Built geospatial retrieval for branch and ATM lookup with geo_shape and geo_distance, including a decay function tied to driving time rather than straight-line distance
Designed multi-tenant routing with per-tenant quotas, strict mappings, and governed component templates so product teams could share clusters without one bad mapping taking down a neighbor
Split volatile fields from stable fields into paired indices to stop full-document reindexing on every balance update — bulk indexing throughput went from 90K to 310K docs/sec
Chased a six-week-old OOM problem down to unbounded fielddata on a text field, capped the parent circuit breaker, and standardized the fleet on G1GC with 31 GB heaps
Profiled write thread pool rejections during month-end batch loads and re-sized bulk queues per index class. The 3 AM pages the ingest team had lived with for a year stopped.
Extended Elasticsearch with a custom Java plugin exposing an internal tokenizer for account and routing number formats, because the query DSL had no clean way to express it
Published node blueprints and a capacity planning model covering shard size, heap-to-data ratio, and IOPS per data node — architecture review now requires it before any new cluster is funded
Codified cluster provisioning in Terraform with ECK on EKS, which took new-environment stand-up from 3 weeks of tickets to a 2-hour pipeline run
Replaced a polling scraper with a Kafka-backed ingest path using Logstash, Beats, and ingest-node pipelines. Events stopped disappearing whenever a broker restarted.
Instrumented the fleet with Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry traces so a slow query can be followed from the API gateway down to the specific shard that ate the time
Presented quarterly search strategy to the CTO's architecture council and won funding for a dedicated ML node tier by walking them through the GPU cost curve in plain terms
Mentored 9 senior engineers through an internal Elasticsearch certification track; 2 of them now own production clusters of their own
Ran monthly working sessions with Elastic product and support contacts on ES|QL and semantic_text, and filed upstream issues that landed as fixes in later 8.x releases
Orchestrated LLM calls in Python with LangChain, adding a retrieval budget and a citation check so the assistant declines to answer when the evidence is thin
